findings.section: What this distillation does not cover
findings.claim: Jones's post-1980 evidence collapse and the KLOC-power-law mythology question whether Scrum's evidentiary base supports the claims practitioners make for it ... For the evidence base, reach for jones-evidence-based-sweng-software-business.md.

findings.evidence: jones deep 175, 193-197: the KLOC scaling finding concerns Halstead and McCabe folklore metrics, not Scrum. Deep 149 (Ch 5.4.3): Jones says the rarity of measurement data for agile processes means the book 'has little to say about them'.
findings.fix: correct: Jones reads software-engineering claims against measurement data (post-1980 evidence collapse; folklore metrics) and notes the rarity of such data for agile processes. For how much evidential weight a Scrum claim can bear, reach for Jones.

findings.section: What this distillation does not cover

findings.fix: correct: The 'WIP is a liability' line carries the shortlink ap.tips/toc with no named referent. For Theory of Constraints as such, OpenStax Accounting Vol 2 cites Goldratt in Ch 1.5 and ranks products by contribution margin per unit of the constraining resource.

notes: Deep ref and converted source read in full; all quotations checked against the source. The most serious error runs through five places (Phase 1 question, What-to-Look-For row 1, anti-pattern row 1, worked example Phase 1, and more softly Concept 4): the distillation recommends reframing external commitments to the Sprint Goal ('Goal-level commitments survive'), and at line 192 calls this 'The Field Guide rule' — but the source's signature position is that the Development Team 'cannot and must not make a firm commitment to delivering the entire Sprint Backlog or even the Sprint Goal'. Other cross-corpus claims fail: Letaw has no Conway's Law or scaling content; Accounting Vol 2 has no TOC chapter or cost-of-quality framing; Jones says it has little to say about agile processes; five 'once projected' distillations already exist. The worked example's board-slide figures (Capacity-adjusted Velocity 28 SP over 25-31 SP / 43-50 days) reuse the source's example data; as hypothetical figures they are FAITHFUL, and 28 is closer to the true arithmetic (27.2) than the source's stated ≈30 (see decision-making notes). The added 'What this distillation does not cover' section is outside the nine-section template (protocol, 'don't add new sections'); noted, not graded.
